title: An ordinary day
goal: Describe your daily routine from getting up to going to bed, use reflexive verbs, and put time expressions in order.
bekal: describe the activities of a whole day in order
use reflexive verbs: *jeg vasker mig*, *hun skynder sig*
wave: Go back over **Unit 7** first: order a full lunch for two people, out loud, with *jeg vil gerne have* and *må jeg få*.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Hvordan ser din dag ud?
dialogs.intro: In class, the teacher asks each student to describe their ordinary day. It's Budi's turn.

lines.speaker: Læreren:
lines.text: Budi, fortæl om din dag. Hvornår står du op?
lines.id: Budi, tell us about your day. When do you get up?
lines.literal: Budi, tell about your day. when stand you up?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Jeg står op klokken halv syv. Så vasker jeg mig og barberer mig.
lines.id: I get up at half past six. Then I wash and shave.
lines.literal: I stand up clock-the half seven. then wash I myself and shave myself.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Ja, jeg plejer at spise rugbrød med ost. Og drikke kaffe.
lines.id: Yes, I usually eat rye bread with cheese. And drink coffee.
lines.literal: yes, I tend to eat rye-bread with cheese. and drink coffee.

lines.speaker: Læreren:
lines.id: How do you get to the university?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Jeg cykler. Det tager tyve minutter.
lines.id: I cycle. It takes twenty minutes.
lines.literal: I cycle. it takes twenty minutes.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Også når det regner. Jeg er dansker nu.
lines.id: Even when it rains. I'm a Dane now.
lines.literal: also when it rains. I am Dane now.

lines.speaker: Læreren:
lines.text: Godt svar! Hvad laver du om aftenen?
lines.id: Good answer! What do you do in the evening?
lines.literal: good answer! what make you in evening-the?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Jeg laver mad, læser lidt og ser fjernsyn.
lines.id: I cook, read a bit and watch TV.
lines.literal: I make food, read little and see far-sight.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Og klokken elleve går jeg i seng. Men jeg falder først i søvn klokken tolv.
lines.id: And at eleven I go to bed. But I don't actually fall asleep until twelve.
lines.literal: and clock-the eleven go I in bed. but I fall first in sleep clock-the twelve.

notes: **At stå op** = to get up, literally "to stand up". Danish has lots of two-part verbs like this, just like English phrasal verbs: *at stå op*, *at gå ud*, *at komme ind*, *at tage af sted*. The second part (*op*, *ud*, *ind*) can't be dropped without changing the meaning.

**Jeg vasker mig** — literally "I wash myself". Danish uses the reflexive here where English usually drops it ("I wash"). If you drop *mig*, the sentence needs another object: *jeg vasker tøjet* (I wash the clothes).
**Jeg plejer at spise** = "I usually eat". *At pleje at* + base form is the most natural way to talk about habits, and it's used more than *normalt* or *som regel*.
**Det tager tyve minutter** — *at tage* is used for duration, exactly like English *to take*.
**Jeg cykler.** Danish has its own verb for cycling, and that's no accident: Copenhagen has more bikes than people. *At cykle* is used as often as *at gå*.
**At lave mad** = to cook, literally "to make food". Everyday Danish has no single verb for "to cook"; *at koge* specifically means to boil.
**At falde i søvn** = to fall asleep, literally "to fall into sleep" — the same picture as in English. Don't confuse it with *at sove* (to be asleep) and *at gå i seng* (to go to bed).
**Først** here doesn't mean "first" but "not until": *jeg falder først i søvn klokken tolv* = I don't fall asleep until twelve. This use is very common and often confusing.

grammars.title: Reflexive verbs
body: Some Danish verbs must carry a pronoun pointing back to the subject. English often manages without ("I hurry", "we sit down"), so this part is easy to forget.
after: Note the third person — singular and plural — uses the special form **sig**, not *ham* or *hende*. It's a close relative of *sin/sit/sine* from Unit 5, and the rule runs parallel: *sig* always points back to the subject.

The most common ones: *at vaske sig* (to wash), *at skynde sig* (to hurry), *at sætte sig* (to sit down), *at klæde sig på* (to get dressed), *at glæde sig til* (to look forward to), *at more sig* (to have fun), *at føle sig* (to feel), *at kede sig* (to be bored).
⚠️ *Jeg glæder mig til weekenden* = "I'm looking forward to the weekend". Danes say this almost every day — it's one of the most useful phrases you can learn.

grammars.title: Order of adverbials: manner — place — time
body: When a sentence has more than one adverbial, Danish has its own standard order. It's close to English, but Danish is stricter, so it's worth practicing.
after: Remember the short form: **MPT** — manner, place, time.

But the time expression can move to the **front** of the sentence for emphasis — and when that happens, the subject jumps behind the verb: *Om morgenen **kører hun** med bus til arbejde.* This jumping rule gets the full treatment in the next unit.

blocks.text: Read this column out loud from top to bottom, then cover it and describe your own day. It's the first really long speaking exercise in this course.
*At tage af sted* (to set off) is one of the most common expressions and one of the hardest to guess from its parts. Learn it whole.

⚠️ In a statement these words stand **after** the verb: *Jeg cykler **altid** til skole.* English puts them before (*I always cycle*), so *jeg altid cykler* is the mistake English speakers make most — and it sounds wrong immediately.

blocks.title: Practice that turns this unit into a skill
items: Describe your day yesterday — but in the present tense, since the past tense only arrives in Unit 17. Ten sentences, in order, out loud.
Then repeat it, this time with a how-often word in every sentence: *Jeg står **altid** op klokken syv.*
Then repeat it again, this time about someone else: *Han står op…* Notice the verb doesn't change at all. Feel how economical this language is.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the right reflexive pronoun (mig, dig, sig, os, jer).
items: Jeg vasker ____.
Hun skynder ____.
Vi sætter ____.
Du glæder ____ til weekenden.
De morer ____.
I klæder ____ på.
I get up at half past six.
I usually eat rye bread for breakfast.
I cycle to the university every day.
In the evening I cook and watch TV.
At eleven I go to bed.
I'm looking forward to the weekend.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite in the right manner–place–time order.
items: hver dag / cykler / jeg / til skole
om morgenen / kører / med bus / hun / til arbejde
om aftenen / spiser / hjemme / vi / sammen
hver uge / arbejder / på en café / han
om søndagen / går / i parken / de / en tur

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
items: op / klokken / står / syv / jeg
mad / laver / aftenen / om / jeg
seng / går / i / elleve / klokken / jeg
skole / cykler / til / altid / jeg
til / glæder / weekenden / mig / jeg

answers: mig — sig — os — dig — sig — jer

Jeg står op klokken halv syv. — Jeg plejer at spise rugbrød til morgenmad. — Jeg cykler til universitetet hver dag. — Om aftenen laver jeg mad og ser fjernsyn. — Klokken elleve går jeg i seng. — Jeg glæder mig til weekenden.
Jeg cykler til skole hver dag. — Hun kører med bus til arbejde om morgenen. — Vi spiser sammen hjemme om aftenen. — Han arbejder på en café hver uge. — De går en tur i parken om søndagen.
Jeg står op klokken syv. — Jeg laver mad om aftenen. — Jeg går i seng klokken elleve. — Jeg cykler altid til skole. — Jeg glæder mig til weekenden.
